My Price is My Life | Setting Sail with Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley and James O’Keefe Episode #4

Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley comes aboard the Lucky Charm III to share what her life’s been like since she heroically exposed how the federal government was handling (and allegedly hiding) adverse reactions to the COVID-19 vaccine.

In 2021, Jodi was a nurse at the Phoenix Indian Medical Center, a facility under the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). She tells James how the Holy Spirit prompted her to hit “record” while her concerned colleagues, including physicians, were discussing patients they believed were suffering adverse effects from the vaccine, reactions that weren't being formally reported. Thus, igniting Jodi’s ongoing advocacy in nursing.

Jodi also shares other challenging moments in her life that strengthened her faith and trust in God, leading her to the work and mission she’s tackling now.

Trading is simpler than most make it out to be — but only if you do the real work:  

1. Stop chasing instant wealth.  
2. Embrace randomness — it’s always present.  
3. Pick one setup.  
4. Delete the other five.  
5. Risk less than you’re comfortable with.  
6. Cut your position size in half.  
7. Then cut it in half again.  
8. Stop watching PnL while trades are open.  
9. Set your risk before you enter.  
10. Never move a stop loss further away.  
11. Know your actual win rate.  
12. Know your true average risk-reward.  
13. Know your worst historical drawdown.  
14. Be emotionally ready for twice that.  
15. Step away when tired.  
16. Step away when emotional.  
17. Step away after revenge impulses.  
18. Don’t trade to feel busy.  
19. Don’t trade to fight boredom.  
20. Learn to do nothing.  
21. Learn to miss moves without reacting.  
22. Accept you’ll never catch every move.  
23. Accept FOMO is self-sabotage.  
24. Don’t increase size after wins.  
25. Don’t increase size after losses.  
26. Journal your emotions, not just entries.  
27. Recognize your tilt pattern.  
28. Identify what triggers self-sabotage.  
29. Remove the trigger.  
30. Build a consistent daily routine.  
31. Prioritize sleep.  
32. Train your body.  
33. Manage caffeine wisely.  
34. Breathe before pulling the trigger.  
35. Separate self-worth from PnL.  
36. Let go of needing to be right.  
37. Accept losses calmly.  
38. Let winners run — as planned.  
39. Stop micromanaging trades.  
40. Backtest with at least 200 trades.  
41. Forward test with small size.  
42. Prove consistency before scaling.  
43. Scale up slowly.  
44. Never scale based on emotion.  
45. Track results in R-multiples, not dollars.  
46. Focus on process — not outcomes.  
47. Measure execution quality.  
48. Grade your performance weekly.  
49. Fix one mistake at a time.  
50. Avoid jumping between strategies.  
51. Avoid indicator overload.  
52. Avoid over-optimizing.  
53. Don’t copy random traders.  
54. Build conviction with data.  
55. Trade one session.  
56. Trade one instrument.  
57. Master one timeframe.  
58. Understand volatility context.  
59. Define when *not* to trade.  
60. Clarify exact invalidation rules.  
61. Accept missed opportunities.  
62. Respect your max daily loss limit.  
63. Stop trading when you hit it.  
64. Stop trading after emotional spikes.  
65. Review trade screenshots daily.  
66. Analyze losers more than winners.  
67. Check if you’re cutting winners too early.  
68. Check if you’re holding losers too long.  
69. Fix execution imbalances.  
70. Protect capital aggressively.  
71. Treat capital like inventory — not profit.  
72. Master position sizing math.  
73. Respect compounding.  
74. Avoid all-in bets.  
75. Avoid “this is the one” thinking.  
76. Trade like a statistician.  
77. Build drawdown tolerance.  
78. Accept flat months.  
79. Accept slow growth.  
80. Accept boredom.  
81. Build patience deliberately.  
82. Train focus daily.  
83. Reduce dopamine dependency.  
84. Stop comparing yourself constantly.  
85. Stop hunting for holy grails.  
86. Accept: you’re the main variable.  
87. Accept: psychology > entries.  
88. Accept uncertainty — permanently.  
89. Protect the downside first.  
90. Scale only after proven consistency.  
91. Never trade to recover losses.  
92. Never trade to prove something.  
93. Never trade to escape reality.  
94. Trade only to execute your plan — nothing more.  
95. Stay small until you’re stable.  
96. Prioritize survival over speed.  
97. Build emotional stability before increasing size.  
98. Respect your system — even when bored.  
99. Think in years, not days.  
100. Stay in the game long enough for probability to work.
